assumptions: The repository selected on GitHub holds the landing page copy the product's visitors read.
Public threads about the product exist on at least one chosen platform within the window; when they do not, insufficient data is the correct result.
A copy fix reaches visitors only after the founder approves it in Decisions and website.change merges it.
effects: Writes the plan reports/feedback-to-fix/{run_id}/PLAN.md in this project.
For a patch, records one copy fix in Decisions; approving it starts website.change, which opens the pull request. The run itself opens none.
cost_drivers: The number of threads and comments opened, at most 30 threads, which grows with the window and platforms chosen.
Running the repository's own lint and test commands on the scratch copy.

rubric.question: Is every quote exactly what the page says, with a link to the comment or thread it was read in?
Does every theme the plan acts on have at least two different people behind it, counted from the quotes?
Do the people behind a planned theme point at the same passage, not just the same file?
Does the plan avoid usernames and put no one's words on the site?
Does every changed sentence say only what the Feature map or the code shows the product does?

cases.description: Two launch threads where different people say the first screen is confusing and ask what to start with; the repository has a hero section and a first-run screen.
Boundary: one person misreads the hero tagline and another objects to the pricing note further down the same landing page file. Different copy is not one theme, so nothing is planned.
Boundary: a single commenter raises three separate points across a thread. One person is not a theme, so nothing changes.
Plausible but unusable input: the chosen platform cannot be opened at all. It must say so and must not fill the plan from memory.
